items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: He just came on down there, and we told him, I said, I want you to take a, you come in on this part.

ctx.x: Yeah. So, when we got, we made the record, I was down there at the old Italian Hall on Espinay. And they had, what they call a master disc, about this big. The electric, I think, had just about come out then, you know. And the hardest thing we had was getting the drums, not to be too loud, and the album morgan on the bass. And when we got down there, that's when I met Sidney Arden. I had been seeing him around, and I heard him play, and that guy's a terrific player. He could play just like, there was very few…
You had the tippies, where did that come from?

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: In fact, I didn't know he was there until I got to where we were at the Italian Hall.

ctx.x: But he fitted in pretty well, don't he?

Oh, he did, yeah, because we didn't have no rehearsal with him. In fact, I didn't know he was there until I got to where we were at the Italian Hall. But I haven't seen him around and known him around, you know, but he fit in right because those two numbers that we rehearsed good, he fit right in there very well.
That's the kind of numbers you play for the people at the Astoria.

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1979-12-05
items.q: Lee Collins, that's when I recorded that thing they called it, Astoria Hot 8. We had Sid Averdino clan, that white man.

ctx.x: And you were playing banjo at this time?

At that time I was born for the Stikker Steamboat Company. Uh-huh. And there was a ten piece band. It had three sax, three brass, and four rhythms. And you had to play banjo, you had to play pangeline guitar. If you were bass, you had to play bass following and bass horn. I worked with, I started with Fate Marble, and then they had a job with Sidney Desveen, and that's where he came to me. We used to play at the country club on Sundays. And that's where the Captain Vaughan came in and heard the band and I used to…
Yeah, for about ten years. And that's when you.
